facts.fact: Historically, one television commercial cost $30,000 to produce, according to the page's account of why TV went untested.
facts.quote: When one commercial cost $30,000 and the only measurement was a ratings estimate, nobody tested anything

facts.fact: For completion-rate tests, the page recommends a minimum of 5,000-10,000 impressions per variation, with a typical wait of 1-2 weeks, and trusts the result when the gap is 2+ points and stable for a week.
facts.quote: | Completion rate | 5,000-10,000 impressions | 1-2 weeks | Gap is 2+ points and stable for a week |

facts.fact: For QR-scan tests, the page recommends a minimum of 30-50 scans combined, a typical wait of 2-4 weeks, and trusts the result when one variation leads 2:1 or better.
facts.quote: | QR scans | 30-50 scans combined | 2-4 weeks | One variation leads 2:1 or better |

facts.fact: For branded search lift tests, the page recommends at least 4 weeks of trend data, with a typical wait of 4-6 weeks.
facts.quote: | Branded search lift | 4+ weeks of trend | 4-6 weeks | Lift tracks one variation's flight weighting |

facts.fact: For geo-split business-outcome tests, the page recommends a full quarter of data, with a typical wait of 8-12 weeks.
facts.quote: | Business outcomes (geo-split) | Full quarter | 8-12 weeks | Matched-area gap exceeds normal variance |

facts.fact: The page states that at 30,000 monthly impressions, a two-way rotation reaches completion-rate thresholds in two to three weeks, while a four-way split starves every variation.
facts.quote: at 30,000 monthly impressions, a two-way rotation hits completion-rate thresholds in two to three weeks

facts.fact: In the page's worked med spa example, the champion spot's completion rate was 93%.
facts.quote: A med spa's champion spot opens with the owner speaking to camera; completion runs 93%.

facts.fact: In week one of the worked example, the challenger spot had a 95.5% completion rate versus 92.8% for the champion, measured on day seven.
facts.quote: Week one: challenger 95.5%, champion 92.8%, but it's day seven, so nobody calls it.

facts.fact: In week two of the worked example, the challenger completion rate was 95.2% versus 93.0% for the champion, on 9,000 impressions each, a 2.2-point gap.
facts.quote: Week two holds: 95.2% versus 93.0% on 9,000 impressions each, a stable 2.2-point gap that clears the threshold.

facts.fact: In the worked example, QR scans were 19 for the challenger versus 12 for the champion.
facts.quote: QR scans agree directionally (19 versus 12).

facts.fact: The worked example's rotation split impressions 50/50 across the same five zips.
facts.quote: Rotation runs 50/50 across the same five zips.

facts.fact: The page gives a 70/30 impression split as an example of an accidental delivery skew that quietly invalidates a comparison.
facts.quote: a 70/30 accidental skew quietly invalidates the comparison

facts.fact: The page's decision rule is to call a winner only when the leading variation clears the threshold table and holds its lead for a full week of stable delivery.
facts.quote: Call a winner** when the leading variation clears the threshold table and holds its lead for a full week of stable delivery.

facts.fact: Generating a second TV ad variation with Adwave is free and takes about two minutes.
facts.quote: Generating a second variation is free and takes about two minutes with Adwave

facts.fact: The page states that a campaign with 25,000-30,000 monthly impressions supports a clean two-way TV ad test with a two-to-three week read.
facts.quote: A campaign with 25,000-30,000 monthly impressions supports a clean two-way test on a two-to-three week read

facts.fact: The page states that completion-rate TV ad tests typically resolve in one to three weeks once each variation has 5,000-10,000 impressions.
facts.quote: Completion-rate tests typically resolve in one to three weeks once each variation has 5,000-10,000 impressions

facts.fact: The page says response-signal TV ad tests want about a month to run.
facts.quote: response-signal tests want a month

facts.fact: The page says geo-split outcome TV ad tests deserve about a quarter to run.
facts.quote: geo-split outcome tests deserve a quarter

facts.fact: The page recommends one test at a time per campaign as the meta-rule for TV ad A/B testing.
facts.unit: test per campaign at a time
facts.quote: one test at a time per campaign

facts.fact: The page recommends generating one challenger each month, testing one element.
facts.quote: Each month, generate one **challenger** testing one element (two minutes of work).

facts.fact: The page says a tested playbook of market response becomes available after twelve months of the testing cadence.
facts.quote: Twelve months later you own something no competitor can copy
